fact: 1915年3月11日，英国颁布枢密院令，宣布对德国实施封锁：驶往德国的中立国船舶被押送至协约国港口检查并扣留。这道命令不称「封锁」而称「报复措施」，美国国务院法律顾问兰辛在备忘录中指出，英国刻意回避「封锁」一词，是为避免与1909年《伦敦宣言》关于封锁的规则正面冲突。

sources.title: Historic UK, World War 1 Timeline – 1915
sources.quote: 11 Mar In an attempt to starve the enemy into submission, Britain announces a blockade of German ports. Neutral ships heading for Germany are to be escorted to Allied ports and detained.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State, FRUS: Lansing Papers 1914–1920, Vol. I, Doc. 240（1915年3月20日兰辛备忘录）
sources.quote: To avoid placing themselves in so different [difficult?] a position diplomatically the British Government issued the Order in Council of March 15th carefully avoiding the terms "blockade" in the Order, but in the note of transmittal they not only use the word "blockade" but seek apparently to have this Government adopt the idea that it is a blockade and to discuss it from that standpoint.

fact: 1915年5月7日下午，丘纳德公司客轮卢西塔尼亚号在爱尔兰南岸外被德国U-20潜艇击沉，船上1959名乘客与船员中1198人溺亡，其中有128名美国公民；该船载有约173吨步枪弹药与炮弹。从被击中到沉没约20分钟。事件在美国引发强烈反应，但美国政府当时仍维持中立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Lusitania
sources.quote: In May 1915 the Lusitania was returning from New York to Liverpool with 1,959 passengers and crew on board. ... on the afternoon of May 7 the vessel was attacked. A torpedo struck and exploded amidships on the starboard side, and a heavier explosion followed ... Within 20 minutes the Lusitania had sunk, and 1,198 people were drowned. The loss of the liner and so many of its passengers, including 128 U.S. citizens, aroused a wave of indignation in the United States ... The Lusitania was carrying a cargo of rifle ammunition and shells (together about 173 tons)

sources.title: Naval History and Heritage Command, Ensuring the Lifeline to Victory
sources.quote: especially when the sinking of the British liner Lusitania by U-20 on 7 May 1915 resulted in the deaths of 1,198 people, 128 of them U.S. citizens.

fact: 1915年5月21日，《每日邮报》抨击陆军大臣基钦纳对西线炮弹短缺负有责任，引爆「贝壳危机」；5月25日，阿斯奎斯把自由党政府改组为联合政府，保守党入阁。军需不足与内阁改组在两周内相继发生。

sources.title: Alpha History, World War I timeline
sources.quote: May 21st: The London Daily Mail launches a scathing attack on war secretary Lord Kitchener, blaming his mismanagement for a shortage of artillery shells on the Western Front. This marks the beginning of the 'Shell Crisis'. ... May 25th: Following the criticism and controversy of the Shell Crisis, British prime minister Asquith reforms his cabinet, assembling a coalition government with several Conservatives.

sources.title: Historic UK, World War 1 Timeline – 1915
sources.quote: 25 May The British Prime Minister Herbert Asquith reorganises his Liberal government into a coalition of the political parties.

fact: 1915年6月，英国设立军需部（Ministry of Munitions），由劳合·乔治出任首任军需大臣；政府下令兴建日产能达800吨无烟火药的巨型工厂，并把其他工厂国有化、转产炮弹。此后英国炮弹产量增幅超过1000%。

sources.title: Alpha History, Total War
sources.quote: Government control of the economy increased dramatically in 1915, in the wake of the 'Shell Crisis' ... A new portfolio was created: the Ministry of Munitions, filled initially by future prime minister David Lloyd George. Construction of a massive factory capable of producing 800 tons of cordite a day was ordered, while other factories were nationalised and retooled for the production of artillery shells. British production of shells increased by more than 1000 per cent.

sources.title: Alpha History, World War I timeline
sources.quote: June 16th: The Chancellor of the Exchequer, David Lloyd George, is appointed to head the newly formed Ministry of Munition and resolve the shortfall in artillery shells.

fact: 1915年9月25日，英军在洛斯发动进攻，首次大规模使用基钦纳新募集的志愿兵，也首次使用氯气（约140吨）；因风向变化，部分毒气被吹回己方战壕。战斗至9月28日平息，协约国退回原阵地，伤亡约5万人，其中2万名官兵没有已知坟墓。

sources.title: Historic UK, World War 1 Timeline – 1915
sources.quote: 25 Sept Battle of Loos starts. This marks the first time that the British use poison gas in the war. It also sees the first large-scale deployment of Kitchener's Army. Just prior to the attack, British troops release 140 tons of chlorine gas into the German lines. Due to shifting winds however, some of the gas was blown back, gassing British soldiers in their own trenches. ... 28 Sept Fighting at the Battle of Loos subsides, with Allied forces retreating back to where they began. The Allied attack cost 50,000 causalities, including three divisional commanders. 20,000 officers and men who fall in the battle have no known grave.

fact: 英国1914年8月8日《国土防卫法》（DORA）赋予政府审查新闻与邮件、无审判拘禁、以军事法庭审判平民、征用土地与建筑的权力。1915年随战事延长追加管制：实行夏令时以延长工时，缩短酒馆营业时间并稀释啤酒，禁止点燃篝火与放飞风筝（可能招引飞艇），禁止向动物投喂面包、禁止在婚礼上撒米。

sources.title: Alpha History, Total War
sources.quote: A week after the declaration of war, the parliament at Westminster passed the Defence of the Realm Act. This legislation empowered the government to secure the nation from internal threat or invasion, by handing it wide-ranging powers, including censorship, the authority to imprison without trial and the power to court martial and execute civilians. ... As the war progressed, new restrictions were added to the legislation. Daylight saving was introduced to provide more working hours in the day. Alcohol consumption was restricted, opening hours of pubs were cut back and beer was watered down to reduce its strength. It became illegal to light bonfires or fly kites, both of which might attract enemy airships.

sources.title: Alpha History, Total War（食品段）
sources.quote: Food became so valuable that it was a criminal offence to feed bread to animals or to throw rice at weddings.

fact: 据英国贸易委员会1915年9月23日在下院的答复，4磅面包的主导零售价：1914年9月1日全英平均6便士，1915年9月1日为8便士（涨2便士）；伦敦西区与中区从6.25便士涨到8便士。同年6月1日全英为8.5便士，9月回落至8便士。另有统计称到战争第一年末曼彻斯特的生活费上涨约35%。

sources.title: Hansard, HC Deb 23 September 1915 vol 74 cc580-1W, Bread Prices（贸易委员会主席 Runciman 答复）
sources.quote: I.—COMPARISON OF PREDOMINANT PRICE OF BREAD per 4 lbs. at 1st September, 1914 and 1915. ... London: N. & N.W 7¾ 6 1¾ ... W. & W.C 8 6¼ 1¾ ... Great Britain 8 6 2 II.—COMPARISON OF PREDOMINANT PRICE OF BREAD per 4 lbs. at 1st June and 1st September, 1915. ... Great Britain 8½ 8 ½

sources.title: The Great World War: A History, Vol. IV（1915年伦敦版，Internet Archive 全文）
sources.quote: In Manchester it was estimated that by the end of the first year of war the cost of living had risen by some 35 per cent. For many of the poorer classes this inevitably meant a reduction both in the quality and the quantity of the food consumed ... Wages rose proportionately as labour grew scarcer.

fact: 1915年6月，英国发行第二次战争公债，利率4.5%，募得9.01亿英镑；其中1760万英镑来自1914年3.5%公债的转换，另有1.38亿英镑来自2.5%与2.75%统一公债持有人转投。政府承诺：若日后发行更高利率的公债，4.5%持有人亦可转换。

sources.title: Wikipedia, War loan
sources.quote: It was followed by £901 million of a second War Loan in June 1915, at 4.5%. £17.6 million of this was accounted for by conversion of the 3.5% issue, and a further £138 million by holders of 2.5% and 2.75% Consols, who were also allowed to transfer to the higher interest rate. The government also pledged that if they issued War Loans at even higher interest, holders of the 4.5% bonds might also convert to the new rate.

fact: 1915年9月，英国下院通过第七次战争拨款2.5亿英镑，使开战以来的拨款总额达到12.62亿英镑（约63.1亿美元）；首相警告战费已达每日逾500万英镑。同期对英法的5亿美元级贷款正在纽约谈判（1915年9月28日宣布，见 US 包）。

sources.title: Commercial and Financial Chronicle, 1915-10-02, Vol. 101 No. 2623（FRASER 全文）
sources.quote: The credit was for £250,000,000 and was the seventh vote of credit that has been adopted in the Commons since the outbreak of the war. The new vote brought the total up to £1,262,000,000 ($6,310,000,000). The Premier warned his hearers that although the war expenditure was now averaging more than £5,000,000 a day

fact: 1915年2月英国成立「陆地舰委员会」（Landships Committee），由海军部主持；7月22日把两履带方案委托给林肯的农业机械厂 William Foster & Co.，8月11日开工，9月9日首台样车「林肯一号机」（即「小威利」）在惠灵顿铸造厂院内试车。这是世界上第一辆完成的坦克原型。1916年2月军方订购100辆改进型Mark I。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, tank (military vehicle)
sources.quote: The first tracked armoured vehicle was improvised in July 1915, in Britain, by mounting an armoured car body on a Killen-Strait tractor. ... A series of experiments by this committee led in September 1915 to the construction of the first tank, called "Little Willie." ... it was accepted by the British Army, which ordered 100 tanks of this type (called Mark I) in February 1916.

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Tanks and Tank Warfare
sources.quote: In February 1915, the government formed the Landships Committee ... The very first tank to be built in the world was the No. 1 Lincoln Machine which was designed by Sir William Tritton (1875-1946) and Lieutenant Walter Gordon Wilson (1874-1957). It was known as "Little Willie" and was designed and constructed between August and September of 1915.
